content:
This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will officially launch to all users on Monday, September 14.

Additionally, the company stated that two features from the iOS 27 beta have been removed and will be reintroduced later through a "future software update" on iPhone: the suggested feature in Messages, and the automatic password-changing feature.

Apple updated its official website this week to reflect that these two features have been temporarily pulled from iOS 27. The changes also apply to other platforms, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users had previously discovered that the automatic password-changing feature was removed in iOS 27 beta 5, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm this change.

A refresher: the suggested feature in the Messages app allows users to add items to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with one tap, based on the content of their conversations.

Below is Apple's description of the password feature:

"The Passwords app will try to go directly to sites where the user has weak or compromised passwords, and update them automatically. At WWDC, Apple explained during its presentation that the feature would use Apple Intelligence and Safari to 'perform actions on the user's behalf in an agent-like manner.'"

There is currently no announcement on when these two features will return alongside iOS 27. Apple's official website only indicates that they will be available in a "future software update."
